newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close easier, follow U.S. lower.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close easier, follow U.S. lower.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended easier on Tuesday, as investors decided to sell and take profits following yesterday's strength, analysts said.
"The market's just giving that back today," said MMS International fixed income analyst Rob Palombi.

Canada's 30-year benchmark bond slipped C$0.19 to C$107.20 to yield 7.374 percent while the U.S. 30-year dipped 13/32 to yield 7.10 percent. The spread between the two narrowed to 27 basis points from 31 basis points at Monday's close of trading.
Monday's market was boosted by unexpected strength in the Canadian dollar.
Canada's weekly T-bill auction today was not very well bid as investors looked to commercial paper to provide better rates of return, said Technical Data analyst Jeoff Hall.

"The short tend is very volatile right now because of the currency," Hall said. Canada's currency weakened to two-year lows last week amid worries the U.S. Federal Reserve will hike rates in May, perhaps prompting similar moves by the Bank of Canada.
Investors are awaiting more direction from U.S. economic data, due out this week. "The market's basically on hold until the (U.S. March) retail report on Friday," Palombi added.

In other prices, the Government of Canada's 10-year benchmark bond dropped C$0.19 to C$101.13 to yield 6.837 percent while the U.S. bond fell 9/32 to yield 6.89 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to a negative spread of five basis points from four basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.16 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.24 percent.
